- Select Duplicate.
- The duplicated program will appear in the Drafts tab.
- From the Drafts tab, click the More Actions icon next to the duplicate program and publish or edit as needed [S1].

stratified_examples.question: How can I add and set up a range slider in my CMS to filter content by a number value?
stratified_examples.candidate_answer:
To add and set up a range slider in your CMS to filter content by a number value, follow these steps:

- Navigate to the page or section where you want the filter.
- Click **Add Elements** on the left side of the editor.
- Select **Input**, then **Slider**.
- Scroll to **Range Sliders** and drag the desired range slider onto the page.
- Click the **Connect to CMS** icon on the range slider.
- In the **Connect Range Slider** panel, select **Filter content**.
- Choose the dataset connected to the elements you want to filter (e.g., repeater, gallery, table).
- Select the number field visitors will use to filter content.
- Optionally, add a new field to your collection if needed.
- Set the filter condition:  
  - **Between**: shows items with values between the slider handles.  
  - **Outside of**: shows items with values outside the slider handles.

This setup allows visitors to filter content dynamically based on the number range selected [S1][S2].
stratified_examples.gt_answer:
To add and set up a range slider in your CMS to filter content by a number value, follow these steps:

1. **Go to your editor**: [Access your editor](https://manage.wix.com/account/site-selector/?actionUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wix.com%2Feditor%2F%7BmetaSiteId%7D%3FeditorSessionId%3D%7Besi%7D%26).

2. **Add the range slider input element**:
   
   1. Go to the page or section where you want visitors to filter content by a number value.
   2. Click **Add Elements** ![](https://d2x3xhvgiqkx42.cloudfront.net/65d5031a-8d20-483c-b08f-0a758e1cf2fd/68a0236f-77f4-43c6-931f-8298ae691a9e/2022/11/17/01f24c8b-2ea3-4d06-a26d-9975a43d617e/a79e245b-4870-4444-ba82-248eca4eb9a7.png) on the left side of the editor.
   3. Click **Input**.
   4. Click **Slider**.
   5. Scroll down to **Range Sliders**, then click and drag the relevant range slider onto the page.

3. **Connect the range slider to the CMS**:
   
   1. Click the **Connect to CMS** icon ![](https://d2x3xhvgiqkx42.cloudfront.net/12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab/d6b40156-9694-4cfe-9209-54815ef9d6dc/2023/06/16/2d484f5d-e1bf-4d48-9e42-82216e8b88de/08e74518-edad-42f8-b007-c974ba767eb6.png) on the range slider.
   2. Select **Filter content** in the **Connect Range Slider** panel on the right.
   3. Click the **Choose a dataset** drop-down and select the same dataset that connects to the elements (e.g., repeater, gallery, table) that you want visitors to filter.
   4. Click the **Filter content by** drop-down and choose the number field that visitors will use to filter the content.

   **Tip:** To add a new field to your collection and use it for filtering content, select **Add new field**, then enter the field name and click **Add**. You can add content to the field in your CMS collection later.
   5. Click the **Condition** drop-down and select the relevant condition:
      
      * **Between:** Show items that have a connected number field value that is between the range slider handles.
      * **Outside of:** Show items that have a connected number field value that is outside of the range slider handles.

4. **Customize the range slider element**:
   
   * Click **Settings** to customize the following:
     
     + **Field title:** Edit the name that displays on the range slider and lets visitors know what it does.
     + **Slider type:** Choose a continuous or stepped slider type:
       
       - **Continuous:** Visitors can select any value within the set range.
       - **Stepped:** Visitors can select specific, incremental values within the set range. Set up the following options:
         
         * **Set steps by:** Click the drop-down and choose how you want to set the steps:
           
           + **Number of steps:** You choose how many steps appear in the range slider. Enter the number of steps in the **Steps** field.
           + **Step value:** You choose the value increments of each step, up to 100. Enter the value of the increments in the **Value** field.
         * **Value labels:** (Optional) Enter a prefix in the **Prefix** field to have it appear before the value (e.g., $). You can also enter a suffix in the **Suffix** field to have it appear after the value.
   * Click the **Layout** icon ![](https://d2x3xhvgiqkx42.cloudfront.net/12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab/d6b40156-9694-4cfe-9209-54815ef9d6dc/2024/04/24/1e3a7616-1ca3-40ad-9e94-d2e18bfd4b98/33c4ffdc-7138-462f-b6e2-4d6505f6f8f6.png) to adjust the following:
     
     + The size and shape of your range slider handles.
     + The track height (thickness) of the track that the handles slide on.
     + Choose a **Left to right** or **Right to left** range display direction.
     + Adjust the alignment, offset, and spacing around the field title.
     + (Steps only) Choose a layout: **Lines** or **Dots**.
   * Click the **Design** icon ![](https://d2x3xhvgiqkx42.cloudfront.net/12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab/d6b40156-9694-4cfe-9209-54815ef9d6dc/2024/04/24/d44e4657-75f7-476b-a92f-c0ed3bc775bc/4d1470bd-bd1d-4d8b-ac9d-5015333e2742.png) to choose a preset design and customize it further.

5. **Click Preview** to test your range slider.
6. **Click Publish** if you are ready to make the changes go live.

**Important:** The range slider is not available in Editor X or the Studio Editor.
